answer: Here is one mechanism that works: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because bridge only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, copper is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any prism approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
